objects.description: One entry in a structure's own record of what its leadership did. Append-only: read newest-first, never re-ordered, never updated and never deleted.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Monotonic storage key, minted from a sequence. It is the tiebreaker when two acts share an instant, so it must increase with time.

fields.name: structure_id
fields.description: The structure whose log this entry belongs to. Required: an act with no structure has no log to land in.

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.description: When the act happened, which is not when the row was written. The primary sort key.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What was done. Every kind carries a class; a kind with no class arm is refused at the write rather than landing with a null class.

fields.name: class
fields.description: The filter grouping this kind belongs to. Stored rather than computed at read time so filtering by it is an index scan.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Who acted. Empty means the timer acted, which is a real state rather than a missing value.

fields.name: actor_label
fields.description: The actor's name and role class as they read at the time, so the row keeps rendering after either changes.

fields.name: actor_structure_id
fields.description: The structure the actor was acting from, which is not always the structure the log belongs to.

fields.name: subject_ref
fields.description: What the entry is about as the reader sees it. Text rather than a foreign key, so it keeps rendering after the object is retired, re-parented or revoked.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: The subject object's id where one exists. Loose on purpose: the log outlives what it describes.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: The composed human sentence and its structured keys. Absence must round-trip as a true null, because two years after occurred_at the free-text keys are stripped and an empty object would make an aged-out row look like it still carried them.

fields.name: escalation_level
fields.description: How far a case was escalated. Set on case_escalated only, so null is the ordinary state.

fields.name: to_structure_id
fields.description: The structure a transfer or escalation went to.

indexes.name: structure_newest
indexes.description: The log's own read: one structure's entries, newest first.

indexes.name: class_since
indexes.description: The per-class tally over a window, and the class filter on the log itself.

objects.description: One entry in the organization's audit trail of everything done to its data as data. Append-only, for structure_act's reason.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Monotonic storage key, minted from a sequence. The tiebreaker within one instant, and the key GetEvent reads by.

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.description: When it happened. The primary sort key.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What was done to the organization's data. Every kind reaches a chip; one that reaches none is refused at the write.

fields.name: chip
fields.description: The filter grouping this kind reaches. Stored rather than computed, for class's reason.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Who acted. Empty means the system, or a vendor operator who has no row in this database at all.

fields.name: actor_label
fields.description: The actor's name as it read at the time.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: The human sentence. Prose rather than a document, unlike a structure act's detail.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description: The checkable artifact: a checksum, a key-id transition, a duration, a diff. Absence must round-trip as a true null, so a row with none is drawn as an em dash rather than as an empty object.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: What the entry is about, loosely.

indexes.name: chip_newest
indexes.description: The log's read, narrowed to a chip, and the per-chip tally over a window.

objects.description: One export build, either the organization's own register or one actor's self-export. The row is never deleted, even once its file is gone.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers and always minted by the store.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Which of the two exports this is. Every rule on a job branches on it, and a job is one or the other and never both.

fields.name: subject_actor_id
fields.description: Whose data the file holds, at actor scope. Required there and refused at organization scope.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description: The administrator who asked for it, at organization scope only. An administrator is never the requester of an actor's own export.

fields.name: requested_at
fields.description: When it was asked for.

fields.name: snapshot_at
fields.description: The instant the build reads from. Never defaulted from requested_at: a zero here is a build that would read now() instead of one instant.

fields.name: include_ids
fields.description: Whether identity numbers are in the file. Refused at actor scope in any form.

fields.name: format
fields.description: How the file is written. An actor's export is always csv_zip, because a pg_dump of one actor's rows is a format only the organization could open.

fields.name: datasets
fields.description: Which datasets the file covers, as a list of names.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the build is. interrupted is a first-class state rather than an absence — it is what lets a resume be a resume.

fields.name: progress_pct
fields.description: How far the build has got, 0..100. Live while building and null before it starts.

fields.name: resumed_from_pct
fields.description: The percentage this run continued from, 0..100. Write-once: it is the evidence for 'continued from 68 per cent, not restarted', so a second interruption must not re-label the job a fresh one.

fields.name: row_counts
fields.description: The per-dataset tally so far, as a map of dataset name to count. Replaced on each advance rather than merged.

fields.name: bytes
fields.description: The finished file's size. Null until it completes.

fields.name: checksum
fields.description: What the collected file is verified against. A completion without one is not a completion.

fields.name: storage_path
fields.description: Where the file was written.

fields.name: file_removed_at
fields.description: When the file was removed. Null while it is still there; the row itself survives either way.

fields.name: file_removed_due_at
fields.description: When the file becomes due for removal, which is always snapshot_at plus the retention window.

indexes.name: scope_newest
indexes.description: The organization's listing and one actor's listing, both newest first.

indexes.name: removal_sweep
indexes.description: The retention worker's walk: files past their due date and not yet removed, oldest first.

objects.description: The record of an operator viewing an actor's contact details. An event rather than a counter: two reads by one operator are two rows.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers and always minted by the store.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Whose contact details were read.

fields.name: read_by
fields.description: The operator who spent the capability.

fields.name: structure_id
fields.description: The structure the operator was acting from.

fields.name: read_at
fields.description: When, to the minute.

fields.name: notified_at
fields.description: When the subject was told. Null until they are.

indexes.name: subject_newest
indexes.description: The subject's own view of who read their details, newest first.

indexes.name: operator_newest
indexes.description: The operator's own side, scoped to themselves.

objects.description: One rendering of one half of the consent sheet, at one version in one language. A version is a fact once published and is never edited in place.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers and always minted by the store.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Which half of the sheet this version belongs to.

fields.name: version
fields.description: The version label, unique within a scope and language.

fields.name: language
fields.description: The language this rendering is in.

fields.name: clauses
fields.description: The clause list, each with a key and its text. A key is stable across versions of the same scope, so a reword reads as a change to that clause rather than a delete plus an insert.

fields.name: effect
fields.description: How each clause changed against the immediately prior version in the same language, as a map of clause key to strengthens, neutral or weakens.

fields.name: translated
fields.description: Whether this rendering has been translated rather than drafted.

fields.name: release_ref
fields.description: The release this version shipped with.

fields.name: copied_mechanics_id
fields.description: The mechanics version this one was copied from, where it was.

fields.name: published_at
fields.description: When it came into force. Null means unpublished, which is an ordinary state rather than an exceptional one.

fields.name: published_by
fields.description: Who published it.

fields.name: superseded_at
fields.description: When a later version took its place. Null on the version currently in force.

indexes.name: natural_key
indexes.description: Scope, version and language together are the natural key. A database constraint rather than a pre-check, so a concurrent caller loses the race in the database instead of slipping past a read-then-write.

indexes.name: in_force
indexes.description: The version currently in force for a scope and language: the greatest published_at with no superseded_at.

objects.description: One actor's acceptance of the consent sheet. Immutable: never updated and never deleted.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers and always minted by the store.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Who agreed.

fields.name: mechanics_version_id
fields.description: The mechanics version they agreed to. Must name a real version.

fields.name: appendix_version_id
fields.description: The appendix version they agreed to, where one is published. Empty is a one-half sheet, which is what an organization that has published no appendix has.

fields.name: agreed_at
fields.description: When they agreed.

fields.name: language
fields.description: The language they read it in.

fields.name: structure_id
fields.description: The structure the record is stamped at, resolved from the actor's live registrations before the record is written.

indexes.name: actor_newest
indexes.description: One actor's consent history, and the current record at its head.
